statusDetail: Coverage complete. Six representative routes/templates were exercised. Category archives and 261 pagination pages were de-duplicated because they share the homepage listing template; the external files2.darkero.com upload application and destructive form submission were not exercised.

page.notes: Server-rendered adult media catalog. No local source was supplied. The working-repo web-uplift.json scopes localhost playground only and was not applied.

paths.description: Homepage listing: primary discovery surface and representative card-grid/listing template.
Search results for “test”: primary content-finding flow and empty/query-state template.
Representative video detail/playback page, including media controls, related content, comments, and download links.
Report Abuse/DMCA route: highest-risk safety and recovery journey.

findings.summary: The theme is effectively hard-coded dark rather than selected from the user’s color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Computed colorScheme is “normal”; the body stays white-on-black, while CSS mentions prefers-color-scheme but does not provide a user-driven light surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark tokens with a stable dark default only when that is an explicit user choice.

findings.summary: A long-running injected animation continues under reduced-motion.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe still reports one running animation with duration 5,500 ms, identical to the normal condition.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential animation and auto-advance inside prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, including third-party creative motion.

findings.summary: High-contrast preferences are not deliberately supported.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules; the increased-contrast screenshot retains the ordinary palette.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations for controls, links, focus indicators, and overlays.

findings.summary: Cross-document navigation swaps instantly with no View Transition support.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition rules or @view-transition declaration across this MPA.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a progressively enhanced cross-document View Transition for route changes, with reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Third-party overlays obscure primary content immediately on load.
findings.evidence: Mobile and desktop screenshots show notification-like, age-confirmation, and “Robot Verification” ads covering the header, card grid, video player, contact page, and abuse-report text.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove load-time interstitial ad units. If age verification is legally required, use a first-party, accessible, clearly branded gate before content and never deceptive ad creative.

findings.summary: Overlay UI is implemented as ad-hoc fixed divs instead of semantic, focus-managed primitives.
findings.evidence: The probe found zero dialog and zero popover elements but multiple fixed overlay divs, including an injected full-surface unit.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal flows and popover for transient UI, with declarative controls, light dismiss where appropriate, focus management, and an accessible close action.

findings.summary: Advertising chrome dominates and repeatedly interrupts the content-first layout.
findings.evidence: Every representative mobile screenshot contains a large ad overlay; the homepage desktop capture also shows an injected ad over the card grid.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove intrusive formats, cap ad density, reserve non-overlapping slots, and keep the first viewport focused on site content.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior relies on global breakpoints rather than container-aware components.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no @container rules, although cards, sidebars, and search controls are reused at distinct sizes.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards/search/sidebar modules containment and size-aware rules, retaining viewport fallbacks where needed.

findings.summary: Many interactive targets are too small for touch.
findings.evidence: The control probe found 64 controls below 24 px in at least one dimension; detail media Play, Mute, and Fullscreen buttons measured 20×20 px. Keyboard outlines exist, but target sizing remains inadequate.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive hit areas to at least 24×24 CSS px, preferably 44×44 on primary mobile controls, without shrinking visible focus indicators.

findings.summary: The primary video-playback journey is obstructed by deceptive overlays.
findings.evidence: The detail screenshot shows the video player covered by a “Robot Verification / Confirm Your Age” ad before the user can reliably play content.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove third-party interstitials from playback and ensure play, pause, seek, download, and back navigation work without detours.

findings.summary: The abuse-report journey has no actionable submission or confirmation state.
findings.evidence: The Report Abuse page contains only plain contact@darkero.com spans, zero mailto links, and no report form, while an overlay obscures the instructions.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a dedicated report form with URL/category/details fields, validation, safe attachment guidance, receipt/reference number, success state, and retry/fallback contact path.

findings.summary: Mobile LCP is slow despite a light first-party page.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 6.0 s and performance 0.74. A separate desktop trace measured LCP 860 ms and TBT 9.24 ms, so the issue is condition-dependent but material on simulated mobile.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or defer ad/push scripts, prioritize only the LCP thumbnail/font resources, and re-test field and mobile lab LCP.

findings.summary: Parser-blocking scripts and styles delay content delivery.
findings.evidence: HAR identified seven parser-inserted high-priority stylesheets plus jQuery, jQuery Migrate, and a third-party ad script as candidates; DOM confirmation shows those head scripts have neither async nor defer.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline minimal critical CSS, consolidate icon styles, defer non-critical first-party scripts, and never parser-block on advertising code.

findings.summary: Large unused third-party JavaScript and unused icon CSS are shipped.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 145 KiB unused JavaScript and 29 KiB unused CSS; two icon stylesheets are 100% unused in the sampled viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused icon packs and push SDK code, conditionally load analytics/ads after consent and need, and eliminate jQuery Migrate if compatibility testing permits.

findings.summary: Listing thumbnails have neither useful alt text nor accessible link names.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 30/30 images with missing alt text; Lighthouse found 30 links without discernible names, matching the image-only thumbnail links.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each thumbnail link the visible card title via text/aria-labelledby and set meaningful concise alt text, or alt="" only when the adjacent accessible title labels the same link.

findings.summary: The primary Search button fails minimum text contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured white #fff on green #0abf53 at 2.44:1, below the required 4.5:1 for normal text.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken the green button background or use dark foreground text while preserving distinguishable hover/focus states.

findings.summary: Media lacks captions and key controls have undersized hit areas.
findings.evidence: The detail probe found a video with no track elements and 20×20 px Play, Mute, and Fullscreen buttons; viewport scaling itself is not disabled and the layout reflows without horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Add captions/transcript or a documented equivalent and enlarge media-control hit areas while preserving mobile reflow and user zoom.

findings.summary: Deprecated platform APIs and cookie inspector issues are present.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse best-practices score is 0.58, reporting three deprecated API warnings and a Cookie issue spanning ad/tracking resources; BFCache itself passes.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or replace the offending third-party scripts and monitor DevTools Issues and deprecation reports in release checks.

findings.summary: Important support and safety pages omit meta descriptions.
findings.evidence: The Contact and Report Abuse probes show unique titles but meta description is null on both routes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add concise, unique descriptions that explain the contact and abuse-report purpose without exposing sensitive report content.

findings.summary: Security headers are largely absent and analytics/storage cookies are not Secure.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS, nosniff, and framing protection are absent. Three cookies are non-Secure, SameSite=None, and about 400 days long.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS, CSP, nosniff, frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, a stricter referrer policy, and Secure/Lax cookies with proportionate expiry.

findings.summary: The page contacts an excessive, opaque tracking and advertising surface before consent.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 18 third-party origins. HAR recorded 28 third-party requests and 496,381 third-party bytes, including analytics, push, fingerprinting, and ad-auction endpoints; long-lived analytics cookies are set.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove opaque vendors, require explicit consent before non-essential storage/networking, minimize fields and retention, and document each remaining processor.

findings.summary: Injected overlay state is not robust or bounded to its host UI.
findings.evidence: Across independent loads, third-party fixed overlays cover unrelated surfaces including playback, contact, and abuse-report content.
findings.suggestedFix: Isolate or remove third-party injection, reserve bounded slots, and ensure any overlay has deterministic ownership, focus, dismissal, and cleanup.

findings.summary: Ads impersonate messages, reCAPTCHA, robot verification, and age confirmation.
findings.evidence: Screenshots show “Conversations” with a fabricated WhatsApp message and multiple fake verification/age panels over primary content, without clear advertising labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Terminate deceptive ad formats and vendors. Require clearly labeled, non-impersonating creatives and block ads that mimic system messages, security checks, or consent controls.

findings.summary: All sampled thumbnails use legacy JPEG delivery.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 30 legacy-format images and no AVIF/WebP; Lighthouse estimates 56 KiB savings from improved image delivery.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants, preserve responsive srcset/sizes, and keep width/height attributes.

findings.summary: Background ad, push, fingerprinting, and analytics work outweighs the page’s own needs.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 61 requests and 780,253 bytes; scripts account for 532,466 bytes, with repeated XHR/beacon calls to push, tracking, and auction hosts.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unnecessary background vendors and gate remaining analytics behind consent, batching and visibility/idle checks.

findings.summary: Third-party code consumes most transferred bytes before user interaction.
findings.evidence: Third parties transferred 496,381 of 780,253 bytes (64%); 28 requests go off-origin, led by push SDK and analytics scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Set and enforce a third-party byte/request budget, remove push/ad SDKs from initial load, and lazy-load proportionate media only after intent.

Deploy security headers and secure, shorter-lived cookies
Give thumbnails accessible names/alt treatment and fix Search contrast
Improve mobile LCP and resource delivery by deferring/removing ad and legacy scripts
Add captions and enlarge mobile media/navigation targets
Honor reduced-motion, contrast, and color-scheme preferences
Convert image delivery to AVIF/WebP while preserving responsive sources
Use semantic overlays and progressive cross-document transitions
Remove deprecated third-party APIs and add support-page descriptions
